Take-home Exercise 3: Prototyping Modules for Visual Analytics Shiny Application

Author

Chen.PengWei

Modified

March 25, 2025

1. Overview

In this take-home exercise, I will perform a predictive modeling analysis (Decision Tree and Random Forest) for the upcoming group project. Further result will be posted on here.

A dataset used is from this research paper to investigate variables influencing property prices in Korea. The dataset comprises of comprehensive information on the property prices in the Busan Metropolitan City of South Korea for transactions in 2018 to 2019 and 27 variables that influence property prices including characteristics of the property, distance to environmental amenities and local built environments, local demographic characteristics, and season in which the transaction occurred.

3. Data Wrangling 

3.1 Select variables

Remove variables that are not useful for predictive modeling. Geographic data will not be used in this modeling.

Property_data <- Property_data %>% 
  select(!Longitude) %>% 
  select(!Latitude) %>% 
  select(!ID)

3.2 Create summer variable

The categorical data should be encoded before building the decision tree. We keep the other categorical data (like floor and year) becasue they may have meaning in the number.

Property_data$summer <- ifelse(Property_data$Spring == 0 & Property_data$Fall == 0 & Property_data$Winter == 0, 1, 0)

Now check your data set again. There will be 27 variables with the new binary variable summer.

3.3 Rename the variable

In R, it will be better for us using the column name without the blank.

names(Property_data) <- gsub(" ", "_", names(Property_data))

4. Data check

4.1 Outlier

It is not necessary required for decision tree to check the outlier, but recommended to check. Outliers may affect split point selection, especially when the feature range is large. It can be processed depending on the data situation, but the decision tree itself is more robust to outliers.

# 選取數值型欄位
num_cols <- sapply(Property_data, is.numeric)
numeric_data <- Property_data[, num_cols]

# 定義異常值檢測函數
find_outliers <- function(x) {
  stats <- boxplot.stats(x)$stats  
  lower_bound <- stats[1]             # 下界限
  upper_bound <- stats[5]             # 上界限
  outliers <- x[x < lower_bound | x > upper_bound]
  return(outliers)
}

# 繪製箱線圖
boxplot(numeric_data, main="Box Plot for Numerical Data", las=2)

Most of the outlier come from population, which has the meaning for our dependent variable. We will keep these outlier here first.

We also found that the variable Dist. CBD have the extreme big range. It is better to transform by log (X+1).

Property_data$`Dist._CBD` <- log(Property_data$`Dist._CBD` + 1)

4.2 Correlation

Before we do the decision tree, it is required to check the correlation between each variable. But we will let users to choose the variable by themselves in shiny. The default will be the one that we done all the cleaning.

cutoff <- 0.8

num_cols <- sapply(Property_data, is.numeric)
numeric_data <- Property_data[, num_cols]

corr_matrix <- cor(numeric_data, use = "complete.obs")

var_names <- names(numeric_data)

for (i in 1:(ncol(numeric_data) - 1)) {
  for (j in (i + 1):ncol(numeric_data)) {
    cor_val <- corr_matrix[i, j]
    if (abs(cor_val) > cutoff) {
      cat("correlation coefficient between" , var_names[i], "and", var_names[j], 
 round(cor_val, 3), "\n")
    }
  }
}
correlation coefficient between Dist._Green and Dist._CBD -0.93 
correlation coefficient between Top_Univ. and High_School 0.806

Feature selection
choose which one we need to drop

# 訓練簡單決策樹模型，計算特徵重要性
model <- train(
  Property_Prices ~ Dist._Green + Dist._CBD + Top_Univ. + High_School,
  data = Property_data,
  method = "rpart"
)
importance <- varImp(model)
print(importance)

5. Regression Tree

names(Property_data_analysis) <- gsub(" ", "_", names(Property_data_analysis))
set.seed(1234)

trainIndex <- createDataPartition(Property_data_analysis$`Property_Prices`, p = 0.8, 
                                  list = FALSE, 
                                  times = 1)

df_train <- Property_data_analysis[trainIndex,]
df_test <- Property_data_analysis[-trainIndex,]

W

anova.model <- function(min_split, complexity_parameter, max_depth) {
  rpart(`Property_Prices` ~ ., 
        data = df_train , 
        method = "anova", 
        control = rpart.control(minsplit = min_split, 
                                cp = complexity_parameter, 
                                maxdepth = max_depth))
  }

fit_tree <- anova.model(5, 0.001, 10)


visTree(fit_tree, edgesFontSize = 14, nodesFontSize = 16, width = "100%")

Tuning of hyperparameters

printcp(fit_tree)

visTree(pruned_tree, edgesFontSize = 14, nodesFontSize = 16, width = "100%")

modeling measurement and checking the overfitting

The training set R-squared (0.8285) is slightly higher than the test set (0.8239), the difference is about 0.47%, which is very small. In terms of MSE, the test set MSE is slightly higher than the training set, but the difference (0.00167) is also small. In conclusion, the performance of the training and test sets is very close, the model has almost no overfitting, and the generalization ability is good.

R-squared is only 0.8239, and the model’s prediction ability is weak. It is recommended to use random forest or further adjust the parameters.

train_pred <- predict(pruned_tree, newdata = df_train)
test_pred <- predict(pruned_tree, newdata = df_test)

train_mse <- mean((train_pred - df_train$Property_Prices)^2)
test_mse <- mean((test_pred - df_test$Property_Prices)^2)
train_r2 <- 1 - sum((train_pred - df_train$Property_Prices)^2) / 
              sum((df_train$Property_Prices - mean(df_train$Property_Prices))^2)
test_r2 <- 1 - sum((test_pred - df_test$Property_Prices)^2) / 
             sum((df_test$Property_Prices - mean(df_test$Property_Prices))^2)

cat(sprintf("Train MSE: %.6f\n", train_mse))
Train MSE: 0.055219
cat(sprintf("Test MSE: %.6f\n", test_mse))
Test MSE: 0.056887
cat(sprintf("Train R-squared: %.6f\n", train_r2))
Train R-squared: 0.828540
cat(sprintf("Test R-squared: %.6f\n", test_r2))
Test R-squared: 0.823885

Visualization for Desicion Tree

library(ggplot2)
residuals <- test_pred - df_test$Property_Prices
plot_data <- data.frame(Predicted = test_pred, Residuals = residuals)
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Predicted, y = Residuals)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs Predicted", x = "Predicted Property Prices", y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal()
# 載入必要套件
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)


# 1. 預測測試集
train_pred <- predict(pruned_tree, newdata = df_train)
train_sse <- sum((train_pred - df_train$Property_Prices)^2)
train_sst <- sum((df_train$Property_Prices - mean(df_train$Property_Prices))^2)
train_r2 <- 1 - train_sse / train_sst
df_test$Predicted <- predict(pruned_tree, newdata = df_test)

# 2. 預測值 vs 實際值散點圖
tree_scatter <- ggplot(df_test, aes(x = Property_Prices, y = Predicted)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +  # 添加對角線
  labs(
    x = "Actual Property_Prices",
    y = "Predicted Property_Prices",
    title = paste0("R-squared (train): ", round(train_r2, 2))
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 5),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 8)
  )

6. Random Forest

6.1 Building Model

The default is 8:2 for the training and testing data set. The user can choose the seed number and the ratio of training data.

set.seed(1234)

trainIndex <- createDataPartition(Property_data_analysis$`Property_Prices`, p = 0.8, 
                                  list = FALSE, 
                                  times = 1)

df_train <- Property_data_analysis[trainIndex,]
df_test <- Property_data_analysis[-trainIndex,]

training model

# user can choose to set random seed  (default 1234)
# user can choose the tuning method :none, cv, repeatedcv, boot(default)
# user can choose splitrule: variance(default), extratrees, maxstat, beta
# user can choose num of tree :5-200 (200 is default)
# user can choose feature importance :"impurity", "permutation

trctrl <- trainControl(method = "boot", number = 5, verboseIter = TRUE)  # number of boot is default


tune_grid <- expand.grid(
  mtry = 8,  # default
  min.node.size = 3,  # default
  splitrule = "variance"  
)


rf_model <- train(
  `Property_Prices` ~ ., 
  data = df_train,
  method = "ranger", 
  trControl = trctrl,
  tuneGrid = tune_grid,
  num.trees = 200,  
  importance = "impurity" 
)

6.2 check for overfitting

6.2.1 Difference in performance between training set and test set

If the training set performance (such as R-squared) is much higher than the test set, it may be overfitting. The difference is about 2%, showing slight overfitting, but not a big difference.

train_predictions <- predict(rf_model, newdata = df_train)
train_mse <- mean((train_predictions - df_train$`Property_Prices`)^2)
train_sst <- sum((df_train$`Property_Prices` - mean(df_train$`Property_Prices`))^2)
train_sse <- sum((train_predictions - df_train$`Property_Prices`)^2)
train_r_squared <- 1 - train_sse / train_sst
cat("Train MSE:", train_mse, "\n")
Train MSE: 0.002337131 
cat("Train R-squared:", train_r_squared, "\n")
Train R-squared: 0.992743 
cat("difference between test and train R-squared:", train_r_squared - r_squared, "\n")
difference between test and train R-squared: 0.01985979

6.2.3 Out-of-Bag Error

OOB MSE is the error estimate of unseen data. If it is stable as the number of trees increases, the model has good generalization ability. In this figure, the OOB MSE stabilizes after 50 trees and does not increase significantly, indicating that the model is not overfitted. If it is overfitted, the OOB MSE may start to rise after a certain point.
The training set MSE is lower than the OOB and test sets, indicating that the model slightly overfits the training data, but the impact is not significant.

oob_errors <- sapply(seq(10, 200, by = 10), function(ntree) {
  model <- ranger(`Property_Prices` ~ ., data = df_train, num.trees = ntree, importance = "impurity")
  return(model$prediction.error)
})
plot(seq(10, 200, by = 10), oob_errors, type = "l", xlab = "Number of Trees", ylab = "OOB MSE", main = "OOB Error vs Number of Trees")
oob_mse <- rf_model$finalModel$prediction.error
cat("OOB MSE:", oob_mse, "\n")
OOB MSE: 0.009510285

’’’ ##setting option for user to decide if they want to do parameter tuning ##default is simple bootstrap resampling trctrl <- trainControl(method = “none”)

##alternative is (repeated) k-fold cross-validation - user input decision on the value of k and the number of repeats cvControl <- trainControl(##default of 10, range: 3-50 method = “cv”, number = 10)

repeatcvControl <- trainControl(##default of 10, range: 3-50 method = “repeatedcv”, number = 10, ##default of 3, range: 3-10 repeats = 10)

##building of model rf_model <- train(Property Prices ~ ., data = df_train, method = “ranger”, trControl = repeatcvControl, #trControl (refer to above objects created) num.trees = 50, #can consider range of 5 to 200 trees importance = “impurity”, #variable importance computation: “impurity”, “permutation” tuneGrid = data.frame(mtry = sqrt(ncol(df_train)), min.node.size = 5, splitrule = “variance”) #splitrule: “variance” (default), “extratrees”, “maxstat”, “beta” #min.node.size: default of 5 for regression trees #mtry: default is square root of number of variables ) ’’’

評估模型（計算 MSE 和 R²）

mse <- mean((predictions - df_test$Property Prices)^2) cat(“Mean Squared Error (MSE):”, mse, “”)

計算 R²

sst <- sum((df_test\(`Property Prices` - mean(df_test\)Property Prices))^2) sse <- sum((predictions - df_test$Property Prices)^2) r_squared <- 1 - sse / sst cat(“R-squared:”, r_squared, “”) ’’’ ```

  • 有差別：

    1. 重要性分數分佈：回歸樹分數差異大，隨機森林分數更平滑。

    2. 特徵貢獻：隨機森林更均勻地利用特徵，回歸樹過度依賴少數特徵。

  • 一致性：兩模型均認為 Size, Parking, Highest_Floor, Year, Units 是最重要的特徵。

  • 兩模型的前 5 名特徵相同 (Size, Parking, Highest_Floor, Year, Units)，說明這些特徵對預測 Property_Prices 的影響在兩模型中都很重要。

  • 重要性分數差異：

    • 回歸樹的原始重要性分數差異很大 (如 Size 3768.25 vs Bus_Stop 0.48)，反映單棵樹對特徵的依賴程度差異顯著。

    • 隨機森林的重要性分數經過標準化 (最高 100)，分數分佈更平滑，反映多棵樹的平均效應，減少了單棵樹的極端依賴。

’’’ registerDoParallel(cores = 4) # 使用 4 個核心（根據你的電腦調整）

定義多種交叉驗證方法

trctrl_none <- trainControl(method = “none”) # 無交叉驗證（快速，但不評估泛化能力） trctrl_cv <- trainControl(method = “cv”, number = 5, verboseIter = TRUE) # 5 折交叉驗證 trctrl_repeatedcv <- trainControl(method = “repeatedcv”, number = 5, repeats = 3, verboseIter = TRUE) # 5 折重複 3 次 trctrl_boot <- trainControl(method = “boot”, number = 5, verboseIter = TRUE) # Bootstrap 重採樣

定義超參數網格

tune_grid <- expand.grid( mtry = c(2, 4, 8), # 測試多個 mtry 值 min.node.size = c(3, 5, 10), # 測試多個 min.node.size 值 splitrule = c(“variance”, “extratrees”) # 測試不同的分割規則 )

定義一個函數來訓練模型並評估表現

evaluate_model <- function(tr_control, num_trees, importance_method) { rf_model <- train( Property_Prices ~ ., data = df_train, method = “ranger”, trControl = tr_control, tuneGrid = tune_grid, num.trees = num_trees, importance = importance_method )

# 交叉驗證表現 cv_results <- rf_model\(results best_params <- rf_model\)bestTune cat(“Cross-validation results:”) print(cv_results) cat(“Best parameters:”, best_params\(mtry, best_params\)min.node.size, best_params$splitrule, “”)

# 測試集表現 predictions <- predict(rf_model, newdata = df_test) mse <- mean((predictions - df_test\(`Property_Prices`)^2) sst <- sum((df_test\)Property_Prices - mean(df_test\(`Property_Prices`))^2) sse <- sum((predictions - df_test\)Property_Prices)^2) r_squared <- 1 - sse / sst cat(“Test MSE:”, mse, “”) cat(“Test R-squared:”, r_squared, “”)

return(list(model = rf_model, cv_results = cv_results, test_mse = mse, test_r_squared = r_squared)) }

比較不同的分析方式

1. 5 折交叉驗證，num.trees = 50, importance = “impurity”

cat(“=== 5-fold CV, num.trees = 50, importance = impurity ===”) result_cv_50_impurity <- evaluate_model(trctrl_cv, 50, “impurity”)

2. 5 折重複 3 次交叉驗證，num.trees = 100, importance = “permutation”

cat(“=== Repeated CV (5-fold, 3 repeats), num.trees = 100, importance = permutation ===”) result_repeatedcv_100_permutation <- evaluate_model(trctrl_repeatedcv, 100, “permutation”)

3. Bootstrap 重採樣，num.trees = 200, importance = “impurity”

cat(“=== Bootstrap, num.trees = 200, importance = impurity ===”) result_boot_200_impurity <- evaluate_model(trctrl_boot, 200, “impurity”)

比較測試集表現

results_summary <- data.frame( Method = c(“5-fold CV”, “Repeated CV (5-fold, 3 repeats)”, “Bootstrap”), Num_Trees = c(50, 100, 200), Importance = c(“impurity”, “permutation”, “impurity”), Test_MSE = c(result_cv_50_impurity\(test_mse, result_repeatedcv_100_permutation\)test_mse, result_boot_200_impurity\(test_mse), Test_R_squared = c(result_cv_50_impurity\)test_r_squared, result_repeatedcv_100_permutation\(test_r_squared, result_boot_200_impurity\)test_r_squared) ) print(results_summary)

找出最佳分析方式（以 Test R-squared 為標準）

best_method <- results_summary[which.max(results_summary$Test_R_squared), ] cat(“analysis method:”) print(best_method) ’’’
